title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls: Look-Back of the Maintenance Count for the Refrigerant Allowance
content:
For the refrigerant allowance on Repair and Emergency Service Calls, the maintenance count is the number of completed tune-up visits posted to the member's agreement under Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements. These are the agreement's tune-up visit entries recorded as completed visits. How far back the count reaches depends on how long the membership has run.

**Rule.** The maintenance count looks back as far as the membership reaches.

| Member first enrolled, in whole calendar months before the date of handling | Completed tune-up visits counted |
|---|---|
| 24 or more | Those posted to the agreement in the last 24 months |
| 12 to 23 | Those in the last 12 months |
| Fewer than 12 | Those of the agreement's current term only |

**Enrollment date.** The first enrollment is the agreement's enrolled date, which never changes on renewal.

**Visit window.** A visit is within the last 24 or 12 months while fewer than that many whole calendar months have passed from its visit date to the date of handling.

## Questions answered

**A member first enrolled exactly 24 whole months before the date of handling: which visits count?** The completed tune-up visits of the last 24 months, because 24 is "24 or more".

**And a member first enrolled 23 whole months before?** Those of the last 12 months.

**A member first enrolled 11 whole months before?** Only the completed tune-up visits of the agreement's current term.

**Is a visit dated 23 whole months and some days before the date of handling within the last 24 months?** Yes, because fewer than 24 whole calendar months have passed. A visit 24 whole months before is not.

## Example (hypothetical record)

A member first enrolled 30 months ago has completed tune-up visits 4, 10, 16 and 26 months before the date of handling. Three of them fall within the last 24 months (the 4, 10 and 16 month visits), so the maintenance count is 3.
